system.name: Melange congressional staffer network
system.description: The people-only graph below members, built from House and Senate payroll and Quorum directories. Covers identity matching and consolidation, the concurrent-service OVERLAP edge rule, the co-tenure and exposure weights, layer-balanced PageRank, eigenvector and bridging measures, noisy-OR evidence, access uncertainty, and outreach ranking. It is descriptive only: there is no composite influence score.

components.name: Concurrent-service OVERLAP edge rule
components.computes: A person-person edge exists only if two people share a container and their payroll intervals intersect.
components.method: Weight = guaranteed overlap x container proximity kappa (personal office 1.00, committee same side 0.75, unknown 0.60, opposite 0.40, leadership 0.75, admin 0.50). 16.0M of 31.1M candidate pairs rejected for zero overlap. After admin exclusion (v6) 4.66M guaranteed pairs remain. Admin containers carried 70.8% of pairs; degree vs largest office size r = 0.87.
assumptions: Concurrent service in a container indicates a real connection
Sequence is a career trajectory, not a tie
Very large containers are suspected catch-all buckets
empirical_questions: Do co-tenured staffers later appear together in lobbying registrations or office moves more than non-overlapping peers?
How much of staffer degree is explained by container size alone?
components.heading: Concurrent-service OVERLAP edge rule

components.name: Co-tenure weight and workplace exposure index
components.computes: Co-tenure weight = kappa x tier x (1 - exp(-days/365.24)) x shared-role attenuation (0.05). Exposure = sum over workplaces of kappa x alloc_i x alloc_j x integral of 1/max(1, n-1) concurrent headcount; strength = 1 - exp(-exposure/TAU).
components.method: Equal allocation across concurrent workplaces; headcount census of observed people. Shared factors: House 0.02, Senate 0.05.
assumptions: Shared days indicate contact opportunity with diminishing returns
empirical_questions: Does inverse-headcount weighting improve prediction of later co-movement between offices?
components.heading: Co-tenure weight and workplace exposure index

components.name: Layer-balanced PageRank, eigenvector and bridging diversity
components.computes: PageRank (d = 0.85; sensitivity 0.70 and 0.95) on a walk splitting mass equally across active layers, with group-balanced teleport. Per-component eigenvector (diagnostic). Bridging = normalized Simpson diversity of walk mass across target kinds.
components.method: Duplicate support is collapsed by max. No composite influence score.
assumptions: Equal walk mass per layer is a modeling prior
Values are descriptive, with no causal direction
empirical_questions: Does layer-balanced PageRank rank staffers who later become senior staff or lobbyists higher than degree does?
components.heading: Layer-balanced PageRank, eigenvector and bridging diversity

components.name: Staff directory matching and identity consolidation
components.computes: Quorum staffer to office matches, and automatic duplicate-person merges.
components.method: A never-guess name ladder (nicknames, accents, surname + chamber uniqueness). A payroll-evidence pin plus record-pair title threshold >= 8 characters (raised from 6; the removals were bare 'counsel'). The web-reference loop has made 0 automatic merges. Exact-name candidates feed only an exploratory layer.
assumptions: Payroll account identity with a corroborating record pair means the same person
Short title matches are false matches
empirical_questions: What is the precision and recall of the matching ladder against a hand-labelled sample?
components.heading: Staff directory matching and identity consolidation

components.name: Recency and access-uncertainty factor
components.computes: cost = 0.35 + ln2 x years since overlap / 5 + 0.25 x workplace concentration; factor = exp(-cost). Not a probability.
components.method: Exposure-weighted last overlap per joint run.
assumptions: Relationship usability decays with a 5-year half-life
empirical_questions: What is the empirical half-life of former co-worker ties as measured by later joint activity?
components.heading: Recency and access-uncertainty factor

components.name: Noisy-OR evidence combination and outreach ranking
components.computes: Evidence strength = 1 - prod over sources of (1 - max source strength). Outreach candidates are ordered by PageRank, then route cost.
components.method: Noisy-OR is defined but not in the build path.
assumptions: Distinct source systems are independent evidence
empirical_questions: Are evidence sources for the same staffer tie actually independent (error correlation)?
components.heading: Noisy-OR evidence combination and outreach ranking

positions.paul_position: Paul's sources treat staffers as gatekeepers and professional ties as conduits. He does not discuss the overlap rule.
Paul highlighted tie strength and the value of weak ties. There is no annotation on exposure weighting.
Paul notes that more research on forms of centrality is needed.
Paul highlighted LobbyView's lobbyist disambiguation (the John Smith problem) and Kim et al.'s graph clustering for donor identity.
Paul wants relationship decay modeled. No source estimates the half-life of staffer ties.

evidence.title: A hypergraph analysis of the European Commission lobby network
evidence.claim: Projecting meetings onto pairwise cliques inflates nodes that have low hypergraph degree but attend a few large meetings. Within each framework the measures agree (clique coreness C vs Cstak r = 0.93; hypercoreness R vs Rstak r = 0.79); cross-framework correlations are weaker (exact values only in Fig. 6). Separately, edge betweenness correlates 0.74 with meeting size.
evidence.system_side: The co-tenure operator enumerates every concurrent pair inside a payroll container (a clique expansion of a container hyperedge); kappa depends only on container KIND. The 54 admin containers (70.8% of pairs in v5) were excluded by owner ruling 2026-09-07. Container-size normalisation remains an OPEN ruling. The vault records Pearson(degree, largest office size - 1) = 0.8694 for the v5 generation, before the admin exclusion.
evidence.transfer: The mechanism carries over: clique projection of any large hyperedge inflates its members. Magnitudes do not: EC meetings are single simultaneous events, payroll containers are multi-year co-presence. The paper's remedy is a hypergraph-native measure (hypercoreness), not per-edge down-weighting; the project's Katz finding (STATE.md:886-896) is that per-edge reweighting cannot remove a degree artifact under sum-based centrality. Evidence for Paul's open ruling, not a recommendation. The 0.87 figure is pre-admin-exclusion and must carry that label.

evidence.title: A hypergraph analysis of the European Commission lobby network
evidence.claim: Hypergraphs are warranted where coordination or simultaneous interaction of more than two actors matters (p.3, citing prior literature). Clique projection explodes a d-person meeting into d-choose-2 links, so nodes with low hypergraph degree but a few large meetings get inflated coreness; hypercoreness avoids this (p.16-17).
evidence.system_side: The exposure index already divides each shared day by concurrent headcount, using duration / max(1, count-1)^gamma in the Census prefix integrals. In the sidecar closeness math, a pair's contact opportunity therefore shrinks as the container grows, unlike the operator's kind-only kappa.
evidence.transfer: Supports the direction of the correction, not the 1/(n-1) form or the gamma value. The paper never estimates a dilution exponent. The evidence comes from EC meeting attendance and only loosely fits multi-year office co-tenure. It also shows a live inconsistency: the sidecar dilutes by headcount and the scored operator does not.

evidence.title: A hypergraph analysis of the European Commission lobby network
evidence.claim: Core measures computed on the clique expansion diverge from hypergraph-native hypercoreness. The authors say a hypergraph representation is 'more than a minor modeling choice'.
evidence.system_side: PageRank (d 0.7/0.85/0.95) and the component eigenvector run on row-normalized co-tenure strengths, which are pairwise edges derived from container co-presence. Containers are grouping layers, not hyperedges in the operator.
evidence.transfer: The paper compares coreness, not PageRank, so it only implies that walk-based ranks on a projection may diverge from a hypergraph treatment. Under D-025 the ranks are heuristic outputs, not access measures, in either representation.

evidence.title: Measuring the dynamical evolution of the United States lobbying network
evidence.claim: LobbyView's lobbyist name disambiguation is score-based and uncertain. Client matching relies on search-assisted lookup that resolves to third-party directories and fails for defunct firms.
evidence.system_side: A never-guess ladder plus payroll-evidence pins, with record-pair titles and organization strings required to be at least 8 characters.
evidence.transfer: The domains differ: LDA lobbyist names versus congressional payroll staff. Wherever LobbyView lobbyist IDs enter the staffer graph as identities (D-021 allows identity use), treat them as probabilistic merges, not ground truth. The system's ladder is stricter than LobbyView's.

evidence.title: Universal multilayer network exploration by random walk with restart
evidence.claim: Top-ranked nodes can shift as walk parameters change, so stability must be measured for each network rather than assumed. The 125-parameter-set exploration was run on the biological gene and disease network only. Airport top-rankings were highly variable in a supplementary figure (Fig S15) with no parameter-set count stated.
evidence.system_side: Confirmed: a bidirectional row-stochastic walk where each node gives 1/active_layers of its mass to each active layer, split by weight within the layer. Teleport is equal across node kinds. PageRank runs at damping 0.70, 0.85 and 0.95 with L1 distance and top-1000 overlap against 0.85. The equal-layer split is labelled an explicit modeling prior in graph_build.py, not in network_math.py.
evidence.transfer: The operator transfers because both are stochastic walks over typed layers and node kinds. The stability result does not transfer by itself: the paper says stability depends on the network, so the same allocation and teleport sweep must be run on the staffer graph. The paper gives no guidance on which allocation is correct. Outputs remain descriptive connectedness, never access or introduction probabilities (D-025).

evidence.title: Social Network Analysis: An Approach and Technique for the Study of Information Exchange
evidence.claim: Brokerage is a positional property separate from prominence. Actors on a path between networks, or spanning a structural hole between unconnected clusters, control flow between them, and betweenness measures this. A path that spans a structural hole is particularly useful.
evidence.system_side: Staffer graph publishes PageRank at damping 0.85 (sensitivity at 0.70 and 0.95) and a component-local eigenvector. Bridging score is normalized Simpson diversity of row-normalized tie mass across target kinds. No betweenness or Burt-constraint score found in fec/staffer_network.
evidence.transfer: Any span score added must describe graph structure only, not access or introduction probability (D-025). Staffer edges are co-tenure and revolving-door ties, so the paper's control-of-flow wording must not carry over. Payroll container cliques are built in by construction. The r = 0.87 degree versus office size figure was not checked.

evidence.title: Social Network Analysis: An Approach and Technique for the Study of Information Exchange
evidence.claim: Relationship strength is its intensity, for example how many goods are exchanged or how often actors meet, and it can be kept as a value rather than dichotomized. At the tie level, measures combine frequency of contact, duration, intimacy, reciprocal services and kinship, and they depend on context.
evidence.system_side: Co-tenure weight = kappa x tier x (1 - exp(-days/tau)) x attenuation, with tau = 365.2425. Shared-role factor 0.05 attenuates shared titles.
evidence.transfer: Principle only: strength should be valued and duration is one input. The article gives no functional form, time constant or proximity multiplier, so tau and the kappa ladder remain owner design. The kappa ladder values were not located in ranking_math.py and are unverified here. The weight is a heuristic exposure score, not a contact probability (D-025).

evidence.title: Social Network Analysis: An Approach and Technique for the Study of Information Exchange
evidence.claim: Structure is derived from observed relationships, not from a priori classes. The article lists membership in organizations among the a priori classifications it avoids as a basis for groups. Cliques form among similar people and limit nonredundant information. Density is actual over possible links, with n(n-1) possible directed ties (380 for n = 20).
evidence.system_side: Person-person edge requires concurrent service in the same container, weighted by guaranteed overlap times kappa. Admin containers are excluded. Rule of record is the brain note concepts/concurrent-service-overlap-edge-rule.md, which exists. The 1.00 to 0.40 kappa ladder and the 70.8 percent figure were not located and are unverified.
evidence.transfer: The article would treat container co-presence as a membership-based classification, close to the a priori organizational class it warns against, not as an observed exchange. Density and clique statistics inside a container are produced by construction. The article gives no link between co-presence and actual exchange. No edge may be described in influence or access terms.

evidence.title: Computational and Graph-Theoretic Analysis of Legislative Networks: New Zealand's Mental Health Act as a Case Study
evidence.claim: The authors argue against PageRank for legislative networks because its static formulation is sensitive to network growth, citing Mariani, Medo and Zhang 2015. No numerical comparison with PageRank is shown.
evidence.system_side: Staffer PageRank uses damping 0.85 as primary, with sensitivity runs at 0.70 and 0.95, on a layer-balanced transition operator with a group-balanced teleport vector.
evidence.transfer: Weak. The growth critique applies to citation networks, where older nodes accumulate in-links. A co-tenure graph takes the argument only if snapshots across vintages are compared. The paper offers an argument, not evidence. The co-tenure graph description comes from project context and was not checked here.

evidence.title: A network analysis of committees in the U.S. House of Representatives
evidence.claim: Porter et al. normalize shared membership against the count expected if same-size committees were assigned at random (normalized interlock, 1 = chance), so container size does not by itself produce strong ties. The paper does not claim that raw shared membership is uninformative.
evidence.system_side: closeness_math.py: peer exposure adds duration divided by max(1, count-1) raised to gamma (line 83); member exposure adds duration divided by max(1, count) raised to gamma (line 84); _at divides by max(1, count-1) for peers (line 92). Larger concurrent headcount dilutes pairwise exposure. employment_history.py line 83 records admin containers carrying 70.8% of co-tenure pairs in the v5 generation. The r = 0.87 artifact figure was not found in fec/staffer_network.
evidence.transfer: Porter's normalization is an observed-over-expected ratio at the container level. The Melange dilution is a duration-weighted 1/n^gamma on person-person exposure. Different unit and functional form, and Porter gives no basis for the exponent. The output is exposure, not closeness or access (D-025).

evidence.title: Social network group decision making: Characterization, taxonomy, challenges and future directions from an AI and LLMs perspective
evidence.claim: Discount-factor and exponential-decay operators penalize long trust chains, but the drivers of decay (path length, node importance) and their effect on network reliability have not been systematically modelled. Narrative claim only; no decay rate is estimated.
evidence.system_side: Access uncertainty is an exploratory log-cost: cost = 0.35 + ln2 x years since overlap / 5 + 0.25 x workplace concentration, and factor = exp(-cost). The code says this is not a probability. Route hops add -ln(0.8 x strength), so each hop discounts by a fixed factor of 0.8.
evidence.transfer: Only the taxonomy transfers: the system uses a fixed-discount, exponential-decay operator of the kind the review names, and the review confirms that no literature-standard decay rate exists. SNGDM trust is trust elicited inside small expert panels. Staffer edges are dated employment exposure. Neither the 0.8 hop factor nor the 5-year half-life gains or loses support from this paper. Route costs stay heuristic and are never closeness or introduction probabilities (D-025).

evidence.title: Influence maximization in unknown social networks: Learning Policies for Effective Graph Sampling
evidence.claim: A cheap query rule can prioritize which nodes to reveal under a fixed budget. H2 (minimum-degree node among those discovered in the last step) beats CHANGE on voles4 (72.8 vs 58.9), damascus (104.9 vs 95.2) and israel (34.2 vs 30.6), Table 5. The text says H2 picks nodes with higher true betweenness than CHANGE.
evidence.system_side: rank_outreach_candidates orders candidates by published PageRank (damping 0.85), then by origin plus target route cost. Its docstring says an incomplete search must not be read as evidence of no route. No budgeted acquisition policy for choosing which directories or people to resolve next appears in these lines.
evidence.transfer: Usable only as a data-collection priority, judged on graph-completeness metrics. Never judged on spread, access or introduction probability (D-025). Influence language stays barred on revolving-door edges. Any learned policy stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it (DE-062).

evidence.title: The Effects of Congressional Staff Networks in the U.S. House of Representatives
evidence.claim: The tie is a member-member count of senior or policy staffers who worked for both offices in the current or previous two Congresses, undirected and row-standardized (p.11, p.18). Senior-tie LES pooled rho is 0.043, 95% CI 0.0095 to 0.096; senior-only ideology is -0.003, CI -0.029 to 0.020. The future-senior placebo CI of -0.033 to 0.071 overlaps the headline, so homophily is not excluded (p.29).
evidence.system_side: office_moves are directed consecutive-span pairs, emitted with SEQUENCE IS NOT A SOCIAL EDGE and canonical_eligible False. The paper's tie is not a sequence link: it is the undirected co-service count, whose closest analogue in the system is shared_with / pair_people, which has no window. The rule against treating sequence as a person-person edge is still consistent with the paper's caution about homophily.
evidence.transfer: House personal offices, 105th-111th Congresses; observational; member-level outcome similarity, not transmission. The text gives Congress numbers only, so the 1997-2010 window is a calendar inference, not the paper's statement.

evidence.title: The Effects of Congressional Staff Networks in the U.S. House of Representatives
evidence.claim: Only senior and policy staff carry signal. Lower-level staff ties are a placebo with a null LES lag (pooled -0.016, text CI -0.070 to 0.027). Adding policy staff to senior ties weakens the LES lag (pooled 0.013, CI -0.015 to 0.037; Table 2 p.24).
evidence.system_side: shared_staff counts people attached to two or more member offices, with no title filter at the count stage and no time window. SHARED EMPLOYEE and intern titles are dropped only from the top_staff eligible list. shared_with takes top partners from pair_people by count, with no window.
evidence.transfer: Applies if shared_with or shared_staff is ever read as a member relationship signal. The paper's senior-only and 3-Congress specification is the comparison; shipped counts are descriptive only.

evidence.title: The Effects of Congressional Staff Networks in the U.S. House of Representatives
evidence.claim: Ties built over the current plus two prior Congresses carry the LES signal. Narrowing to a two-Congress horizon leaves the senior LES interval barely including zero (-0.0006 to 0.1088; 94% interval 0.0016 to 0.1066). This is window sensitivity, not a decay estimate.
evidence.system_side: Access-uncertainty cost uses a fixed 5-year staleness half-life on years since last joint overlap (staleness = ln2 * age / 5). The file labels its calibration as 'Exploratory log-cost scenarios; not fitted success or friendship probabilities', and the docstring calls the costs assumptions that must not be shown as probabilities.
evidence.transfer: Weak. The paper's window concerns member-member outcome similarity, not whether staffer-staffer relationships remain usable. It cannot calibrate the half-life.
